## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results in this world yet. The starting net scored 0, and the starting net also scored 0 in world 2, where only the reference net with layout hedging succeeded (~0.22). Earlier evidence suggests zeros come from deviations the world doesn't describe, not from the recipe or capacity. So round 1 bets only on what the network assumes, and every candidate keeps the reference recipe. Without data, nothing is ruled out yet. One assumption is safe: the 1x1 stem mixes all obs channels freely, so a permuted channel order cannot by itself cause failure. A transposed or flipped obs relative to the actions is covered by hedging the output layout, because only the relative alignment matters. The candidates are: the reference; the full set of 16 action layouts (8 grid symmetries × type-major or type-minor); a 5x5 head conv for other footprints and anchors; DONE at index 0 or at the end; and two combined maximum hedges. Each file falls back to a Linear mask embedding if n_place ≠ T·Y·X.

### Round 2
All six round-1 nets scored 0 on dev and in training. Ruled out, at the reference recipe: the 16 symmetry × type-order layouts, DONE at index 0, anchor offsets of 1 to 2 cells and footprints up to 5x5. Obs channel order cannot be the cause, because the learned 1x1 stem gives the same result under any channel permutation. What remains open: (1) n_place ≠ n_types·Y·X. Every round-1 file then fell back to the same slow dense Linear head, which would explain a uniform 0. (2) Type-middle action orders (Y,T,X). (3) An arbitrary action permutation. (4) An obs whose memory layout is scrambled (stored as Y,X,C but labelled C,Y,X). (5) A reward scale whose value loss swamps the shared trunk. (6) Harder dynamics that need more receptive field or more samples. Every candidate now adapts its action layout to the spec: K=n_place/(YX) maps, a compact per-footprint anchor layout, or the dense fallback. On top of that, each tests one further bet, and one candidate combines all of them.

### Round 3
Twelve trials, and every one scored 0 on dev and 0 in training. That rules out these deviations: the 24 action layouts (8 grid symmetries times type-major, type-minor and type-middle order), DONE at index 0, the compact per-footprint action layout and a multiple-of-YX action count, a fixed scramble of action indices (dense path), the obs stored channel-last, other anchors or footprints (5x5 head), reward scale (separate critic) and short context (dilated trunk). Obs channel order is already hedged, because the first 1x1 conv mixes all channels. All the hedges so far kept the obs internally consistent, so obs parts that disagree with each other remain untested. If the target and build channels sit in different frames, the net would need a global transform that local convs cannot learn. This round adds two such hedges: all 8 symmetries of the whole obs fed to the 1x1 stem, and learned cell remaps for each channel group. If these also score 0, the deviation is probably reward or dynamics, which the network cannot fix.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and in training. None of these moved the score: 24 action layouts, both DONE positions, 8 obs symmetries, a channel-last obs, learned cell remaps, a 5x5 head, a dense permutation path, a separate critic, a deeper trunk, or 1 epoch with 426k steps. The 1x1 stem can already learn any obs channel permutation, z-order or group swap, so those are ruled out in practice. What remains untested is how inputs and features are represented. Obs values may lie outside [0,1], for example raw heights or a raw step count. The net may lack layer-aware 3D features or footprint statistics for working out where a brick lands under changed dynamics. The reward may be sparse, which needs a longer horizon and a critic that cannot take over the gradient. This is the last round, so each candidate pairs the reference hedge with one of these untested ideas, plus two combinations, so that any nonzero score has the best chance.
